title: Basic-open sections detect quasi-isomorphisms after open-subscheme restriction
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $g\in A$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=D(g)$, and $i:F\to J$ a morphism of integer-indexed complexes of module sheaves [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $R$ be restriction to the localized site over $U$ followed by the canonical equivalence with $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then the $A$-linear map of section complexes $\operatorname{affineOpenSections}(A,U)(i)$ of [def-sc-principal-open-alternating-total] is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if $\Gamma(U,Ri)$ is a quasi-isomorphism over $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, using global sections of [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Neither complex is assumed quasi-coherent, K-injective, or bounded.

source.place: Tag 08D2, A-linear sections on principal opens; Tag 08BS for the open-subspace restriction convention. Explicit restriction-of-scalars identification for the definitions used here.

proof.text: Forget scalars on both section functors to AddCommGrpCat. For any open U, let V be the underlying open of U.overEquivalence.inverse.obj top. Extensionality of opens proves U = V, including U empty. The component of sectionsForgetIso is the original module presheaf applied to the isomorphism op U = op V. The definitions of overFunctor and overEquiv identify its target with the additive group of global sections on the open subscheme. Naturality follows from PresheafOfModules.naturality_apply. Only the section definitions of the cited nodes are used.

Map the natural section isomorphism to integer-indexed complexes. Compose with Mathlib Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso on both sides to compare successive applications of restriction, global sections and forgetting scalars. Arrow.isoMk and quasiIso_iff_of_arrow_mk_iso identify quasi-isomorphism of the two underlying additive chain maps. Each ModuleCat-to-AddCommGrpCat forgetful functor is additive, preserves finite limits and colimits, and reflects isomorphisms. Apply Mathlib HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_map_iff_of_preservesHomology to both sides to recover the stated iff. No quasi-coherence, resolution, boundedness, or nonemptiness hypothesis is used.

proof_origin.place: Tags 08D2 and 08BS, section-restriction comparison; direct Lean implementation N2, 2026-10-13, through underlying additive section functors and Mathlib exact forgetful functor reflection.

lean.statement: theorem principalOpenSections_restriction_quasiIso_iff (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (g : A) (F J : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace)) ℤ) (i : F ⟶ J) : let U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens := PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g let R := SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace) U ⋙ Equivalence.functor (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace).over U)) (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace)) (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U) QuasiIso (((affineOpenSections A U).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map i) ↔ QuasiIso (((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor U.toScheme.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map ((R.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map i))
